channel.title: The Daily Digest
channel.description: One top story from each of my chosen publications, updated daily.

item.title: NYT: U.S. Loses Its Measles Elimination Status, a Historic Setback for American Health
item.description: The nation was once regarded as a global leader for reining in the highly contagious virus. Now, large outbreaks that sicken thousands could become routine.

item.title: NPR: Iran launches third round of strikes on Bahrain, host of U.S. Navy's 5th Fleet
item.description: Iran fired drones on Tuesday at a U.S. radar facility in Bahrain, its third attack in recent days on American military targets in the Gulf island kingdom after a roughly two-month lull in fighting.

item.title: BBC News: Government backs welfare shake-up to prevent 'lost generation'
item.description: Ex-minister Alan Milburn has set out plans to divert spending from benefits towards job support.

item.title: The Guardian: ‘The landslide hit the side of my car. I heard screaming, and realised it was me’ – This is climate breakdown
item.description: She set off for home in bright sunshine in British Columbia, Canada. Then the rains came – and the mud. This is Chelsey Sharpe’s story Location: Agassiz , Canada Disaster: Southern British Columbia floods, 2021 In 2021,…

item.title: Al Jazeera: Mozambique opposition leader goes on trial on terrorism charges
item.description: Mozambique’s opposition leader Venancio Mondlane has gone on trial facing terrorism and civil disobedience charges

item.title: Ars Technica: Humanity braces for an alien invasion in 3 Body Problem S2 teaser
item.description: “Wake up! They haven’t come 24 trillion miles to negotiate. They are coming to exterminate us.”

item.title: WIRED Backchannel: Congratulations to WIRED’s Class of 2026
item.description: This past year was, frankly, crazy. For our inaugural WIRED Yearbook, we celebrate the people, inventions, and viral moments that made it a little more bearable—and are already defining the future.

item.title: WIRED Science: The Dark Side of the Moon Was the Brightest Part of 2026
item.description: Through personality clashes, blaring smoke detectors, and a broken pee vent, the Artemis II astronauts made history—and bonded for life.

item.title: WIRED Business: Jensen Huang Says He’s Open to Coming Back to Nvidia
item.description: Huang said in a statement that he “would be honored” to return as Nvidia CEO if the board of directors supported the decision.

item.title: The New Yorker: How Could an Upgrade Cancel Eighteen Thousand Flights?
item.description: The F.A.A.’s ground stop was one of the worst travel disruptions since 9/11. Here’s what does and doesn’t make sense about the Trump Administration’s story.

item.title: New York Mag The Cut: What Should I Do With All My Mother’s Stuff?
item.description: I’m drowning in her belongings, but it’s hard to let go.

item.title: New York Mag Curbed: The NYC Neighborhoods Where It’s Smarter to Buy Than Rent
item.description: Rents and apartment prices are so high that there’s just a handful of neighborhoods where it’s cheaper to buy than rent over ten years.

item.description: INDIANAPOLIS -- The Indiana Supreme Court has weighed in on the District 45 race in the Indiana State Senate, allowing Indiana State Senator Chris Garten, the announced president pro tempore for the Indiana State Senate…
